subject: Materials Science
title: Sintering: Baking Powder into Solid
description: A quick win: understand Sintering: Baking Powder into Solid.

hook.text: A ceramic part starts as loose powder. Heat it — without melting — and it becomes solid.

buildup.text: Sintering heats powder particles until atoms diffuse across their contact points.

discovery.text: Necks grow between particles, pores shrink, and the piece densifies into a strong solid.

twist.text: The part shrinks 10–20% during sintering — engineers must design the mold oversized.

climax.text: Nearly every ceramic product — tiles, bricks, porcelain — is made by sintering.

punchline.text: Sintering fuses powder without ever reaching the melting point.

quiz.question: What happens during sintering?
options: The ceramic melts and is poured into a mold
Powder particles bond by atomic diffusion below melting point
A liquid adhesive glues the particles together
